record.title: Venezuela-side Pacaraima–Santa Elena crossing closure after US attack, January 3, 2026
record.scope: Venezuelan side of the Pacaraima–Santa Elena de Uairén land crossing
record.direction: Venezuelan-side control affected both directions; phased Brazil-bound tourist returns.
record.movement: Ordinary cross-border travellers and vehicles at this crossing.
record.exceptions: Brazilian tourists were permitted to return before full normalization, according to Folhapress. Uniform denial to all people or goods is not asserted.
record.enforcement: Cones and Venezuelan border guards controlled passage.
record.consequences: Temporary interruption followed by observed pedestrian movement in both directions and Brazilian vehicles entering and leaving Venezuela.
record.relationship: Different year and trigger from AM012 (2019), AM013/R4-AM-001 (January 2025) and the inherited pandemic entry regimes. No duplicate in the full 528-record baseline.
record.status_observation: Status limited to dated evidence; no claim of present closure.
record.official_rationale: Brazilian officials attributed the Venezuelan closure to the US military attack and capture of Nicolás Maduro; no original Venezuelan closure order was retrieved.
record.context: The border restriction was reported on the morning of the attack and lifted during the same day.
record.uncertainty: Reports differ on the number of hours and reopening times. Return permissions preceded general restoration. The record supports same-day bounds, not a single all-persons interval or an exact hour duration.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. Brief phased closure and reopening on January 3, 2026. Exact hours withheld because accounts differ and return exceptions preceded general restoration.
